results.note: Drives okx.fetch_btc_daily_bars(205) across 3 pages (100/100/5, asserted via captured request params) and coinbase.fetch_btc_daily_bars(350) across 2 pages, then asserts exact order equality against the source rows and len(set(...))==len(list) to prove no duplicates at the seams. Covered by the passing `test` gate.

Shortens page 2 by one row for both venues and asserts a real Error with an exact 'returned N bars, expected M' message — okx.py:77-83 and coinbase.py:70-77 implement the check that fires on any page, not just the first.

Deletes exactly the row that sits at the OKX/Coinbase page-1/page-2 boundary. Traced both code paths: OKX (cursor-based) is caught by the cross-page pairwise-timestamp contiguity check at okx.py:97-115 ('not contiguous' asserted); Coinbase (time-window based) is caught by the page-completeness check at coinbase.py:70-77 because the missing row shrinks the window's match count — both are genuine seam-crossing failures, not per-page-only checks, matching the story's explicit note that contiguity must be checked across the assembled series.
Asserts len(result)==250 and timestamps==sorted(timestamps,reverse=True) after a full paginated fetch, i.e. the US-201 'exactly N bars' contract holds post-assembly, not just per page.

Supplies only 249 of the 250 required rows, asserts the result is an Error (not a padded 250-length series) and that the source `rows` list itself was never mutated in place — a genuine synthesis/padding guard, not a tautology.

pytest.mark.integration test calls okx.fetch_btc_daily_bars(250) and coinbase.fetch_btc_daily_bars(250) with no client override, so client=None forces the real httpx.get() path against the live OKX/Coinbase endpoints (okx.py:50-55, coinbase.py:43-49) — genuinely driving the public entry point end-to-end. No pytest.ini marker deselection or addopts filters this out (pyproject.toml:20-26 only registers the marker, doesn't exclude it), so the reported `test` gate (`uv run pytest -q`, exit 0) necessarily executed and passed this live test too. The implementer's own handoff note claims it 'fails loud' in their sandbox due to blocked sockets, but the gate that was actually run for this judgement passed, which is the authoritative signal per the rules.

note: All 6 criteria map 1:1 to real, non-tautological tests named exactly as the story specifies.
